## Today

**Question:** Can we build the Rosling chart and make it move?

| Step | What we do |
|------|-----------|
| 1 | Join two tables with a key |
| 2 | Pivot a summary table: long to wide and back |
| 3 | Draw the Gapminder graphs |
| 4 | Animate the Rosling chart |

Data: `band_members` and `nycflights13` for joins, the Gapminder table from class 6 for the rest.

---

# 1. Joins {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**Put two tables together**

---

## Two tables and one key

```{r}
# Who is in which band
band_members
```

```{r}
# Who plays which instrument
band_instruments
```

The key is `name`. Mick has no instrument. Keith has no band.

---

## left_join(): keep every row of the left table

```{r}
band_members |>
  left_join(band_instruments, by = "name")
```

Mick stays, with `NA` for the instrument. Keith disappears.

---

## inner_join(): keep only the matches

```{r}
band_members |>
  inner_join(band_instruments, by = "name")
```

Mick and Keith both disappear.

---

## full_join(): keep every row of both tables

```{r}
band_members |>
  full_join(band_instruments, by = "name")
```

---

## Two joins that only filter

```{r}
# semi_join: rows of the left table that have a match
band_members |>
  semi_join(band_instruments, by = "name")
```

```{r}
# anti_join: rows of the left table that have no match
band_members |>
  anti_join(band_instruments, by = "name")
```

---

## Which join? {.smaller}

| Join | Keeps | New columns |
|------|-------|-------------|
| `left_join()` | all rows of the left table | yes |
| `inner_join()` | rows with a match in both | yes |
| `full_join()` | all rows of both tables | yes |
| `semi_join()` | rows of the left table with a match | no |
| `anti_join()` | rows of the left table without a match | no |

Start with `left_join()`. It never drops rows of the table you care about.

---

## The key has a different name in each table

```{r}
band_instruments2
```

```{r}
#| error: true
# The column is called artist here, not name
band_members |>
  left_join(band_instruments2, by = "name")
```

---

## join_by() matches two different names

```{r}
band_members |>
  left_join(band_instruments2, by = join_by(name == artist))
```

---

## A real case: flights and airlines

```{r}
# flights has the carrier code only
flights |>
  select(carrier, flight, dep_delay) |>
  head(3)
```

```{r}
# airlines holds the name of each code
airlines |>
  head(3)
```

---

## Add the airline name

```{r}
flights |>
  select(carrier, flight, dep_delay) |>
  left_join(airlines, by = "carrier") |>
  head(4)
```

---

## Check the row count after a join

```{r}
# A left_join must keep the 336,776 rows of flights
flights |>
  left_join(airlines, by = "carrier") |>
  count()
```

More rows mean the key repeats in the right table. Fewer rows mean the join dropped rows.

---

## Join, then split, apply, combine

```{r}
# Mean departure delay by airline name
flights |>
  left_join(airlines, by = "carrier") |>
  group_by(name) |>
  summarize(mean_dep_delay = mean(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_dep_delay)) |>
  head(5)
```

---

## Airports: the key has two names again

```{r}
# dest in flights, faa in airports
flights |>
  select(dest, dep_delay) |>
  left_join(airports, by = join_by(dest == faa)) |>
  select(dest, name, dep_delay) |>
  head(4)
```

---

## Which destinations have no row in airports?

```{r}
flights |>
  anti_join(airports, by = join_by(dest == faa)) |>
  distinct(dest)
```

## Gapminder: a summary table to join back

```{r}
# Mean life expectancy of each continent in 2007
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  group_by(continent) |>
  summarize(continent_life = mean(life_exp))
```

---

## Join the summary to every country

```{r}
# Which countries are far below their continent mean?
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  left_join(
    here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
      read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
      filter(year == 2007) |>
      group_by(continent) |>
      summarize(continent_life = mean(life_exp)),
    by = "continent"
  ) |>
  mutate(gap = life_exp - continent_life) |>
  select(country, continent, life_exp, continent_life, gap) |>
  arrange(gap) |>
  head(5)
```

---

# 2. Pivots {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**Long and wide tables**

---

## Long: one row per continent and year

```{r}
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year %in% c(1952, 1982, 2007)) |>
  group_by(continent, year) |>
  summarize(life_exp = weighted.mean(life_exp, population), .groups = "drop")
```

A reader cannot compare the years at a glance.

---

## pivot_wider(): one column per year

```{r}
# names_from: the column whose values become column names
# values_from: the column that fills the cells
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year %in% c(1952, 1982, 2007)) |>
  group_by(continent, year) |>
  summarize(life_exp = weighted.mean(life_exp, population), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = life_exp)
```

---

## The wide table lets us calculate across columns

```{r}
# Backticks: the column names are numbers
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year %in% c(1952, 1982, 2007)) |>
  group_by(continent, year) |>
  summarize(life_exp = weighted.mean(life_exp, population), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = life_exp) |>
  mutate(change = `2007` - `1952`) |>
  arrange(desc(change))
```

---

## pivot_longer(): back to long

ggplot needs the long shape.

```{r}
# cols: the columns to stack. -continent means all columns except continent
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year %in% c(1952, 1982, 2007)) |>
  group_by(continent, year) |>
  summarize(life_exp = weighted.mean(life_exp, population), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = life_exp) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -continent,
    names_to = "year",
    values_to = "life_exp"
  )
```

---

## The year is now text. How to get a number?

```{r}
# names_transform = as.integer turns the text into a number
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year %in% c(1952, 1982, 2007)) |>
  group_by(continent, year) |>
  summarize(life_exp = weighted.mean(life_exp, population), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = life_exp) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -continent,
    names_to = "year",
    values_to = "life_exp",
    names_transform = as.integer
  ) |>
  head(4)
```

---

## Which shape? {.smaller}

| Task | Shape |
|------|-------|
| Plot with ggplot2, group, filter, join | long |
| Show a table to a reader who compares columns | wide |
| Calculate a difference or a ratio between two years | wide |

## Your turn 5 {background-color="#d5e8d4"}

**Take the wide table back to long and draw one line per continent.**

```{r}
#| eval: false
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year %in% c(1952, 1982, 2007)) |>

  geom_line(linewidth = 1)
```

# 3. Gapminder graphs {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**From many lines to the Rosling chart**

---

## One line per country

```{r}
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = life_exp, group = country)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.3)
```

`group = country` draws one line per country.

---

## Which lines belong to which continent?

```{r}
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = life_exp, group = country, color = continent)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.4)
```

---

## One panel per continent

```{r}
# facet_wrap() splits the plot in panels
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = life_exp, group = country)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~ continent)
```

---

## Rosling, step 1: two numbers

```{r}
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = income, y = life_exp)) +
  geom_point()
```

Most countries sit on the left. The rich countries stretch the axis.

---

## Rosling, step 2: a log axis

```{r}
# A log axis gives each doubling of income the same width
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = income, y = life_exp)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_log10()
```

---

## Rosling, step 3: size and color

```{r}
# size = people, color = continent
# scale_size_area() makes the circle area proportional to population
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = income, y = life_exp, size = population, color = continent)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 15)
```

---

## Rosling, step 4: labels, theme and readable colors

```{r}
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = income, y = life_exp, size = population, color = continent)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 15) +
  scale_color_viridis_d() +
  labs(x = "Income per person", y = "Life expectancy", title = "2007") +
  theme_minimal()
```

---

## Two years, two panels

```{r}
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year %in% c(1952, 2007)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = income, y = life_exp, size = population, color = continent)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 12) +
  scale_color_viridis_d() +
  facet_wrap(~ year) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Panels show two years. Twelve years need another idea.

# 4. Animation {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**Time on the screen instead of in panels**

---

## gganimate: one new line

`transition_time(year)` draws one frame per year and moves the circles between frames. The text `{round(frame_time)}` in the title shows the current year.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = income, y = life_exp, size = population, color = continent)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 15) +
  scale_color_viridis_d() +
  labs(title = "Year: {round(frame_time)}", x = "Income per person", y = "Life expectancy") +
  theme_minimal() +
  transition_time(year)
```

---

## Lines that grow: transition_reveal()

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  group_by(continent, year) |>
  summarize(life_exp = weighted.mean(life_exp, population), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = life_exp, color = continent)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_color_viridis_d() +
  theme_minimal() +
  transition_reveal(year)
```

## Recap {.smaller}

| Task | Code |
|------|------|
| Keep all rows of the left table | `left_join(x, by = "key")` |
| Keys with different names | `join_by(a == b)` |
| Find rows without a match | `anti_join()` |
| Long to wide | `pivot_wider(names_from, values_from)` |
| Wide to long | `pivot_longer(cols, names_to, values_to)` |
| One line per group | `group = country` |
| Panels | `facet_wrap(~ continent)` |
| Animation | `transition_time(year)` |
